modules.name: Deliverables, hard-rules and deadline tracker
modules.design_question: Which VTC hard rules, recommended deliverables and upload prerequisites are met, missing or at risk, and how long remains before the 30 Nov 2026 closing instant (23:59 London)?
inputs: brief_register: the team's copy of the brief PDF with its SHA-256, plus transcribed rules {id, value, exact|max, page, transcribed_by, checked_by}
board_layout from P13-M06a (frames, element tags, panel count)
export_manifest from P13-M06b (bytes, px, ratio, sha256, subsampling, scan mode, checks[], anonymity_findings[])

editable checklist: 6 hard rules (JPEG, size, panel count, A2 landscape ratio, English, anonymity), 3 process gates (UIC validated, identity verified, two-person sign-off with complete licence pack) and 20 recommended items (3 diagrams: programme, structure, massing; 3 studies: wind, solar/shadow, sustainability; site plan; ground floor plan; 3 typical plans; 2 sections; skyline view; mid-city view; 4 ground-level perspectives; policy reflection)
module result cards from other packets (wind, shadow, sustainability, structure, programme)
rubric gaps from P13-M07 (advisory only)
rights_status from P13-M08a
current UTC time, deadline instant 2026-11-30T23:59:00Z, team time zone
outputs: submission_status (typed JSON: hard_rules[], gates[], coverage, missing[], days_left, blocking, brief_sha256)
blocking_issues list consumed by the release gate P13-M06c
dated rule changelog (Q&A answers after 3 Nov, brief re-reads)

parameters.name: panel_count_rule
parameters.relationship: Terms 4.8 lets the brief set one to four panels. Reading the brief's count as exact flags a 3-board entry; reading it as a maximum passes it. Default is exact 4 (team-supplied) until the PDF is read.

parameters.name: recommended_item_set
parameters.relationship: Each unplaced recommended item lowers coverage. Team mapping to jury criteria: missing ground-level views weakens human-scale evidence (40%); missing wind, solar or sustainability studies weakens design-excellence evidence (20%).

parameters.name: deadline_instant
parameters.relationship: The page gives 23:59 London time (GMT in November) = 2026-11-30T23:59Z = 16:59 Vancouver (UTC-7); Terms 4.7 says 24.00 London. The earlier instant is used because late entries are disqualified (8.4).

parameters.name: registration_close
parameters.relationship: Registration closes 29 Oct 2026 (hour not stated). Upload needs a validated UIC and identity-verified members, so missing the close removes the upload route; the tracker warns as the date nears.

parameters.name: upload_lock
parameters.relationship: After the first upload, edits need a paid reactivation fee (Terms 4.7, 7.7) and the entry may go to early evaluation. Exporting early is safe; uploading should happen once, when every gate passes.

parameters.name: file_size_margin
parameters.relationship: A bigger safety margin below 10 MB protects against MB/MiB ambiguity and portal overhead but forces lower JPEG quality or fewer pixels, which softens thin linework.

parameters.name: aspect_ratio_tolerance
parameters.relationship: A2 is 420 x 594 mm (ratio 1.414); a tighter tolerance prevents stretched or cropped boards, a looser one hides layout mistakes.

parameters.name: language_allow_list
parameters.relationship: The page requires English; a literal check would reject Nation names. Explanatory text must be English, while reviewed names pass with an English gloss. Spellings vary between sources, so each entry is reviewed and Unicode-normalised.

metrics.name: Panel file format
metrics.good: every panel is .jpg/.jpeg
metrics.bad: any PDF, PNG, TIFF or other format
metrics.method: Check extension and JPEG magic bytes of each exported board.
metrics.basis: Buildner Terms 4.8: each panel must be saved as JPEG; non-compliance may lead to disqualification (8.2).

metrics.name: Panel file size (hard limit)
metrics.good: <= 10^7 bytes (stricter reading of 10 MB)
metrics.method: Read byte length of each exported JPEG.
metrics.basis: Terms 4.8 sets 10 MB per panel without defining MB; the tool applies the stricter 10^7 bytes.

metrics.name: Panel file size (team target)
metrics.good: <= 9.5 x 10^6 bytes
metrics.bad: amber between 9.5 x 10^6 and 10^7 bytes; red above 10^7
metrics.method: Same byte count compared with a margin that is safe under either MB definition.
metrics.basis: Team margin; editable.

metrics.name: Panel count upper bound
metrics.good: 1 to 4 panels
metrics.method: Count exported boards.
metrics.basis: Terms 4.8: the brief sets a single panel or up to four panels.

metrics.name: Panel count required by the brief
metrics.good: equals the brief_register value (default exact 4)
metrics.bad: differs from the register, or register empty (amber until the PDF is hashed)
metrics.method: Compare board_layout count with the brief_register panel rule (exact or max).
metrics.basis: Earlier marked verified from team-supplied text; the brief PDF was never opened and Terms 4.8 defer the count to it. Now unverified until the PDF is stored with SHA-256 and two members check the transcription.

metrics.name: Board aspect ratio / orientation
metrics.good: landscape, width:height = 1.414 +/- 0.005 (594 x 420 mm)
metrics.method: width_px / height_px of each JPEG.
metrics.basis: A2 = 420 x 594 mm is verified (ISO 216). The landscape rule rests on the unopened brief (team-supplied), so it is unverified; the tolerance is a team choice.

metrics.name: Language
metrics.good: all explanatory text English; every non-English token on the reviewed allow-list with an English gloss
metrics.bad: non-English explanatory text, or an unreviewed non-English token
metrics.method: Manual attestation per text block (P13-M08b sets language='en') plus allow-list and glyph checks from P13-M06b.
metrics.basis: English-only is stated on the competition page (verified); admitting Nation names through an allow-list is the team's reading, to confirm in Q&A before 3 Nov.

metrics.name: Upload prerequisites (UIC, identity)
metrics.good: UIC validated and every team member's identity verification active
metrics.bad: any member unverified or no UIC
metrics.method: Manual attestation of portal status by two members.
metrics.basis: Terms 3.2 and 3.6 require verification on Architects' Network before UIC validation; the how-to-enter page says it is required before upload.

metrics.name: Registration close warning
metrics.good: > 8 days to 29 Oct, or UIC already validated
metrics.bad: <= 8 days with no UIC: amber; <= 2 days: red
metrics.method: 29 Oct 2026 minus now, shown only while no UIC is recorded.
metrics.basis: Team thresholds; 8 days is the time left on 21 Oct 2026. The closing hour is not stated on the page.

metrics.name: Upload-once gate
metrics.good: first upload only after all hard rules and gates pass and two members sign
metrics.method: P13-M06c unlocks the package only when blocking=false and two sign-offs are logged.
metrics.basis: Terms 4.7: edits after the first upload need a paid fee; the gate itself is tool design.

metrics.name: Recommended-item coverage
metrics.good: 20 of 20 items placed (counts met: 3 typical plans, >= 2 sections, >= 4 ground-level views)
metrics.bad: any category with zero items placed
metrics.method: Match checklist items to tagged board elements in board_layout.
metrics.basis: Item list and minimum counts come from the brief via the team (unverified); items are 'recommended', so a gap is not a rule breach and the cut-off is a team choice.

metrics.name: Days of buffer before closing
metrics.good: >= 7 days between 'all hard rules pass' and the closing instant
metrics.bad: <= 2 days, or any hard-rule failure within 7 days
metrics.method: deadline_instant minus now, shown in London (GMT) and Vancouver (UTC-7).
metrics.basis: Earlier text converted the close to 15:59 PST; BC is on UTC-7, so 16:59. The 7-day and 2-day buffers are team choices; late entries are automatically disqualified (8.4).

metrics.name: Time-zone data check
metrics.good: Intl offset for America/Vancouver at 2026-11-30T23:59Z equals -07:00
metrics.bad: -08:00 or other: browser tzdata predates 2026b, use fixed offset and warn
metrics.method: Format the instant with timeZoneName 'longOffset' and compare with -07:00 at load time.
metrics.basis: tzdb 2026b records BC on permanent -07 from 2026-03-09; no fall-back in Nov 2026.

metrics.name: Brief register integrity
metrics.good: PDF stored with SHA-256 and every rule has a page reference and a second-person check
metrics.bad: any rule without page reference or second check
metrics.method: Validate the register JSON; re-read after Q&A closes on 3 Nov.
metrics.basis: Team control because the brief PDF could not be opened by the spec authors.

visualization: Checklist grid: 20 recommended-item rows x up to 4 board columns with green/amber/red chips; hard rules and gates are pass/fail badges linked to their clause (e.g., Terms 4.8)

Dual-time countdown (London GMT / Vancouver UTC-7) on a timeline with ticks for 29 Oct registration close (amber banner when <= 8 days), 3 Nov Q&A close, 13 Nov course core, 30 Nov 16:59 Vancouver / 23:59 London
Four board thumbnails with ghost slots for missing items and a byte gauge (bytes against 10^7 and the 9.5 x 10^6 target), plus an upload-once panel listing open gates
modules.method: Load a versioned JSON: brief_register, 6 hard rules (JPEG, size, panel count, A2 landscape ratio, English, anonymity), 3 process gates (UIC validated, identity verified, two-person sign-off with complete licence pack) and 20 items with jury tag and minimum count. Hard rules read export_manifest; language is a manual attestation plus glyph and allow-list checks. Coverage = items whose minimum count is met in board_layout tags / 20. The deadline is the UTC instant 2026-11-30T23:59:00Z, shown per zone with Intl.DateTimeFormat (timeZoneName longOffset); if Vancouver is not -07:00 a fixed offset is used and a warning shown. Any rule or gate failure sets blocking=true, which P13-M06c obeys. Every threshold shows its source or an amber 'team assumption' tag; edits are logged; Q&A answers become dated changelog entries.
modules.human_judgment: Reading the full brief and Q&A answers and transcribing its rules twice; whether an item truly answers the brief (a wind study must be an analysis, not a label); deciding which recommended items to omit and justify; the single upload through the Buildner portal and the final sign-off.
modules.limits: The brief PDF is sent by emailed link and could not be opened here; board count, A2 landscape, weights and the 20 items are team-supplied. The portal may apply undocumented checks (pixels, colour mode, MB vs MiB, progressive JPEG); a test upload on the live entry is unsafe because the first upload locks edits (Terms 4.7). Coverage counts presence, not quality.

libraries.name: Intl.DateTimeFormat (browser built-in)
libraries.role: London/Vancouver time conversion with timeZoneName longOffset and the offset self-check

modules.effort: S-M: 4-5 person-days; first delivery 6 Nov (format, size, ratio, panel rule, deadline, gates), anonymity and language checks by 13 Nov

modules.name: Drawing extraction (plans, sections, make2d-style linework)
modules.design_question: Can plans and sections be produced from the model as scaled, layered linework that fits the board frame, including a full-height tower section, and reconciles with programme areas?
inputs: Layer 0 meshes / B-reps with program tags (from imports: Rhino 3dm, OBJ, IFC, SketchUp, Revit)
storey elevations, floor-to-floor heights and below-grade depth (programme / structure modules)
cut plane and section line definitions chosen by user
site north rotation angle (SITE packet)
frame size in mm and target scale from P13-M06a (board_layout)
optional: Rhino Make2D SVG/DXF exported by the user from desktop Rhino (v0 route)
outputs: drawing_set[]: {id, type plan|section|elevation, svg, scale, cut_height, bbox_mm, fit_pct, layers by program tag, line classes} consumed by P13-M06b
gfa_by_storey reconciliation result for programme modules
DXF/SVG export for use in Rhino/Illustrator

parameters.name: cut_height_above_floor
parameters.relationship: Plans are conventionally cut about 1.2 m (4 ft) above finished floor, showing walls, openings and columns; a cut at slab level hides openings, one above head height loses wall and door relationships.

parameters.name: section_line_position
parameters.relationship: A section through the core and public volumes shows how public-facing uses stack vertically through the tower, which the brief asks for; a section through blank floors hides it.

parameters.name: plan_scale
parameters.relationship: Printed extent = real size / n. The 144.8 m block side is 290 mm at 1:500 but 724 mm at 1:200, beyond the 420 mm board height; a smaller scale frees area but shrinks annotation legibility.

parameters.name: section_scale
parameters.relationship: Printed height = H/n. A 305 m tower plus ~20 m below grade (illustration) is 650 mm at 1:500, over the 420 mm board height, and 325 mm at 1:1000; podium sections at 1:200-1:500 need partial cuts.

parameters.name: hidden_lines_on
parameters.relationship: Make2D writes hidden lines to separate layers that can be dashed or switched off. The browser route (three-edge-projection) returns visible edges only, so hidden lines there need a separate differencing pass.

parameters.name: input_route
parameters.relationship: Make2D runs in desktop Rhino; a server needs Rhino.Compute on Windows Server with core-hour billing (US$0.10 per core-hour), so v0 imports its SVG/DXF. The mesh route projects along one axis per view; IFC can use IfcOpenShell on a server.

parameters.name: reconciliation_level
parameters.relationship: Summing areas at the 1.2 m cut measures wall lines and openings; slab-edge loops at floor level track floor area. The zoning floor-area definition is unsourced, so tolerances are team values.

parameters.name: crease_angle_threshold
parameters.relationship: UNRESOLVED: relationship between edge-angle threshold and drawing clarity on curved facades was not found in an opened source (see unresolved_relationships).

metrics.name: Plan cut height convention
metrics.good: 1.2 m (about 4 ft) above finished floor
metrics.bad: cut at slab level (0 m) or above 1.8 m
metrics.method: Compare chosen cut with the convention.
metrics.basis: Good value is the stated convention; the bad bounds are the team's reading of 'approximately'.

metrics.name: Cut-loop closure ratio
metrics.good: 100% of cut polylines closed (poche can fill)
metrics.method: closed cut loops / all cut loops after slicing Layer 0 with the cut plane.
metrics.basis: Open loops indicate non-watertight Layer 0 geometry; thresholds are team-set.

metrics.name: Drawing fits allocated frame
metrics.good: scaled bbox <= 100% of frame in both axes (sections use tower height plus below-grade depth)
metrics.method: bbox_mm = model extent / scale, compared with the frame in mm on a 594 x 420 mm board; shown at preset selection, not only after export.
metrics.basis: Arithmetic: 144.8 m at 1:500 = 290 mm; a 325 m section is 650 mm at 1:500 (over 420 mm) and 325 mm at 1:1000.

metrics.name: Segments per drawing
metrics.good: <= 250,000 line segments
metrics.method: Count after linework simplification.
metrics.basis: No published budget; chosen so rasterising a board stays fast. Tune after testing.

metrics.name: Area reconciliation with programme tags
metrics.good: |slab-edge area - tagged GFA| <= 1% per storey
metrics.method: Sum polygon areas of slab-edge loops at floor level per storey versus Layer 0 tag totals; state the GFA definition used.
metrics.basis: Team tolerance; the Vancouver floor-area definition (zoning exclusions) was not opened, so it is a team assumption until PROG sources it.

metrics.name: Line-weight hierarchy
metrics.good: cut > silhouette > projected edge > hidden with each step about 2:1
metrics.bad: two classes drawn at the same weight
metrics.method: Class-to-weight table rendered in the SVG stroke-width.
metrics.basis: Common drafting convention recalled from ISO 128-20, which was not opened; weights are editable presets.

metrics.name: Line classes available by route
metrics.good: Make2D import: cut, silhouette, tangent and hidden layers; browser edge projection: cut, silhouette, crease and visible only
metrics.bad: hidden class offered on the browser route without a tested method
metrics.method: List the line classes each route actually returns in the drawing_set.
metrics.basis: Earlier text credited Make2D hidden layers to the browser route and cited pdf-lib (S30); three-edge-projection returns visible lines only.

visualization: SVG preview with toggles per line class (cut, silhouette, crease, visible, hidden where available) and per program-tag layer, poche filled with the programme colour
Plan with cut-line markers, rotated site-north arrow and scale bar
Board-frame overlay showing the drawing at 1:n inside the allocated rectangle, with an overflow warning in red
Scale ladder: horizontal bars for printed section height at 1:200, 1:500 and 1:1000 against a vertical line at the 420 mm board height
modules.method: v0 (core): the user exports Rhino Make2D SVG/DXF from desktop Rhino; the tool imports it, maps layers to program tags, fills closed cut loops as poche, scales to 1:n, checks fit against the M06a frame and writes drawing_set. v1 mesh route: 1) index Layer 0 as meshes; 2) plans: slice with a horizontal plane at the cut height, chain segments into polylines, close loops, fill poche; project visible geometry below the cut with three-edge-projection (y-axis); 3) sections and elevations: rotate the scene so the view axis is y, clip at the section plane, repeat; 4) classify lines as cut, silhouette, crease or visible; hidden = all projected edges minus visible (clipper2-js difference, untested prototype); 5) output SVG layered by program tag with scale bar and north arrow rotated by the site angle. Report closure ratio, segment count, area reconciliation and fit. IFC: IfcOpenShell on a server worker (roadmap).
modules.human_judgment: Where to cut and section, which elements and levels represent the design, whether to use partial sections, line weights, annotation and entourage, and whether the drawing actually tells the story of vertical public uses.
modules.limits: Mesh linework is faceted on curved facades; curtain-wall detail and below-slab structure are absent from Layer 0. The edge-projection library works along one axis, shows 12 open issues and outputs visible edges only; performance on a 300 m tower is untested. Make2D needs desktop Rhino or a billed Rhino.Compute server and stays the quality reference.

modules.name: Camera presets and viewpoint library
modules.design_question: From which sourced viewpoints and lenses must the tower be shown (Queen Elizabeth Park skyline, mid-city, four ground-level views), and does the design read at those distances?
inputs: site location and ground elevation, terrain and context models incl. existing and approved towers (SITE packet)
City of Vancouver Open Data 'View cones' polygons (cones 3.2.1-3.2.4)
tower heights and massing from Layer 0
site north rotation angle
sun date/time from CLIM packet for lighting
outputs: camera_preset[]: {name, position_local, georef_origin, target, hfov, roll, shift, viewpoint_source, eye_height, azimuth} consumed by P13-M04, P13-M05, P13-M06b and CLIM image exports
cone_overlay: apex, bearings and polygon intersection with the site footprint
tower_share_of_frame and context_tower_visibility per preset
compass-labelled overlay data (Stanley Park, BC Place, Entertainment District, Burrard Inlet/North Shore Mountains)

parameters.name: viewpoint_position
parameters.relationship: The four cone polygons share an apex at 49.24216 N, 123.11244 W (computed), about 186 m east of Wikipedia's park point. Using the park point shifts the sight line to the tower by up to about 2 degrees at 5 km.

parameters.name: viewpoint_elevation
parameters.relationship: Eye elevation = terrain at the apex (SITE packet) + eye height. Wikipedia's 125 m refers to the park and Little Mountain, not to the apex; a higher eye puts more of the tower above the horizon.

parameters.name: cone_fan
parameters.relationship: Development inside a cone polygon is height-limited (dataset text). The four cones span bearings 341.5 to 19.5 degrees and run 5.5-6.2 km from the apex (computed); overlap with the site must be shown in the skyline view.

parameters.name: viewing_distance
parameters.relationship: Apparent height = atan(height difference / distance). Illustration: a 300 m tower at 5 km subtends about 3.4 degrees, so doubling distance halves its size in frame and forces a longer lens or a crop.

parameters.name: focal_length_equivalent
parameters.relationship: Horizontal field = 2 x atan(18/f): 50 mm gives 39.6 degrees, 85 mm gives 23.9 degrees. Longer lenses enlarge the distant tower in frame but narrow the visible context.

parameters.name: eye_height
parameters.relationship: Ground-level views at about 1.6 m show canopies and podium frontage at pedestrian scale, the scale the human-scale criterion judges; higher cameras read as aerial views.

parameters.name: site_north_rotation
parameters.relationship: The site plan's north arrow is rotated from the street grid, so view azimuths and compass labels must use the rotated north or the labels will point to the wrong landmarks.

parameters.name: local_origin
parameters.relationship: UTM 10N northings near 5.46 million m fall on 0.5 m steps in 32-bit floats (computed), so vertices jitter. Subtract a site-centred origin in double precision before building cameras and meshes.

metrics.name: Tower share of frame height (QE Park skyline)
metrics.good: >= 10% of image height
metrics.method: Project tower top and base to the image plane; (top_y - base_y)/frame height; auto-suggest focal length to reach the target.
metrics.basis: Team legibility target; no source gives a value.

metrics.name: Viewpoint offset from the City cone apex
metrics.good: <= 10 m from the dataset apex
metrics.bad: > 50 m, or a park centroid used (about 186 m off)
metrics.method: Distance between the preset and the apex derived from the view-cones polygons in the local frame.
metrics.basis: Earlier text said the origin was unobtainable. The apex is derived from the open dataset (about 1 m coordinate precision); apex-as-designated-origin is an inference until the Public Views Guidelines are read. Tolerances are team values.

metrics.name: Site intersection with QE Park cone polygons
metrics.good: intersection computed and shown for each of 3.2.1-3.2.4
metrics.method: Clip the site footprint against the four triangles in the local frame; any overlap adds an encroachment note to the skyline caption.
metrics.basis: Polygon geometry from the City dataset (modified 2026-10-19).

metrics.name: Cone ceiling height versus tower top
metrics.good: tower top below the cone ceiling at the site (ceiling value sourced)
metrics.bad: above the ceiling, or ceiling unknown
metrics.method: Compare once ceilings are read from the Public Views Guidelines or confirmed by the City (views@vancouver.ca is the contact in the dataset text).
metrics.basis: The dataset has no height fields; the 2024 Guidelines PDF returned HTTP 403.

metrics.name: Number of ground-level perspectives
metrics.method: Count presets of type ground.
metrics.basis: Earlier marked verified; the figure comes from the unopened brief as supplied by the team, so it is unverified until the PDF is read.

metrics.name: Ground-level eye height
metrics.method: Camera z minus local ground z.
metrics.basis: Common adult eye height; team preset, editable.

metrics.name: Vertical convergence
metrics.good: verticals within 0.5 degrees of vertical (shift lens, zero pitch)
metrics.method: Check camera pitch/roll and lens shift.
metrics.basis: Architectural-visualisation convention; team preset.

metrics.name: Context towers present in the context mesh
metrics.good: every existing and approved tower in the frustum is in the mesh and visible or flagged occluded
metrics.method: Compare the SITE packet tower list with ray-cast visibility from each preset.
metrics.basis: The brief (as supplied) says context includes existing high-rises and future approved towers in the same range.

visualization: Plan map with rotated north arrow, the four QE Park cone triangles drawn from the apex (labelled 3.2.1-3.2.4, site footprint overlaid, overlap hatched), a wedge for each camera and a dashed line of sight to the tower top
Elevation profile from the viewpoint to the site: terrain line, horizon, tower silhouette, context towers
Thumbnail grid with 'tower % of frame' badge and burned-in compass labels
modules.method: Fetch the City view-cones polygons (cones 3.2.1-3.2.4) and take their shared vertex as the viewpoint origin. Convert lon/lat to EPSG:32610 with proj4js in doubles and subtract a site-centred origin before building three.js cameras. Elevation = terrain at the origin (SITE packet) + eye height. Aim at the tower centroid, zero roll, lens shift to keep verticals vertical; choose focal length so tower share meets the target. Clip the site footprint against the triangles and report overlap. Ray-cast camera to tower top and base against context meshes (three-mesh-bvh) to flag occlusion and list context towers in frame. Ground presets sit at the site edges named in the brief (arterial, retail high street, lane or mid-block link, transit plaza and below-grade station entrance), eye height 1.6 m. Output camera JSON and compass labels using the rotated north.
modules.human_judgment: Choosing the mid-city viewpoint, composition, season and time of day; confirming the apex as the designated origin and obtaining cone ceilings; deciding which four ground-level views best show the public realm.
modules.limits: Cone ceiling heights, the Public Views Guidelines text and the policy's amendment status were not read (City guideline hosts returned 403); the dataset gives polygons only and reading the apex as the origin is an inference. Terrain and context come from the SITE packet. Tree canopy and haze at the park are not modelled. The brief does not define the mid-city viewpoint.

modules.name: Viewport conditioning capture (depth, line, segmentation)
modules.design_question: Which exact guides (clay beauty, depth, line, tag-colour segmentation) can be rendered from Layer 0 and context so AI renderings stay registered to the massing and its neighbours?
inputs: camera_preset from P13-M03
Layer 0 and context meshes with program tags and existing/approved tower tags
palette mapping program tag and context class to flat colour
sun vector from CLIM packet
target pixel size
outputs: conditioning_pack: {beauty_png, depth_png, line_png, seg_png, palette_json, camera_json, sun_vector, sha256} consumed by P13-M05
pixel-aligned tower mask and context-tower masks used by the fidelity checks

parameters.name: capture_size
parameters.relationship: gpt-image sizes need multiples of 16, ratio <= 3:1, edges <= 3840 px and 655,360-8,294,400 pixels; above 2560x1440 is experimental. Larger captures keep thin features but raise token cost.

parameters.name: depth_range_normalisation
parameters.relationship: The diffusers examples min-max normalise depth to 0-1 per image, so the near/far range sets how many grey levels the tower receives; a range spanning the whole city leaves the tower few levels.

parameters.name: line_threshold
parameters.relationship: The diffusers example uses Canny thresholds 100 and 200; lower thresholds keep more edges and tighten structural control on the result, higher ones keep only strong outlines.

parameters.name: segmentation_palette
parameters.relationship: The original ControlNet segmentation model expects ADE20K classes; a custom palette (programme tags plus existing, approved and other context) needs a prompt legend or a fine-tuned model to be interpreted correctly.

parameters.name: controlnet_conditioning_scale
parameters.relationship: In diffusers examples a scale of 0.5 is used; higher values follow the guide image more strictly, lower values give the prompt more freedom and risk geometry drift.

parameters.name: sun_vector
parameters.relationship: The sun in the clay capture sets the shadow direction the render is told to follow; an output with a different sun misstates shading and shadow length relative to the CLIM results.

metrics.name: Size rule compliance (OpenAI route)
metrics.good: all five size rules satisfied
metrics.method: Validate width, height, ratio and pixel count before sending.
metrics.basis: OpenAI image-generation guide size constraints.

metrics.name: Registration between passes
metrics.good: 0 px offset (same camera, same render call)
metrics.method: Compare silhouette of the depth, line and segmentation passes.
metrics.basis: By construction; checks protect against resize or crop mistakes.

metrics.name: Tagged-pixel completeness
metrics.good: 100% of tower pixels carry a program tag
metrics.method: Count pixels of the 'unknown' colour inside the tower mask.
metrics.basis: Team threshold.

metrics.name: Context-class completeness
metrics.good: every context tower in frame carries an existing or approved tag
metrics.method: Count towers in the ID pass by class against the SITE packet list.
metrics.basis: Team rule so context towers can be checked in the AI output.

metrics.name: Pack completeness
metrics.good: beauty present (OpenAI route); depth + line + segmentation + beauty present (ControlNet route)
metrics.method: Check files and sidecar JSON.
metrics.basis: Route requirements from the ControlNet guide and OpenAI edit endpoint.

visualization: 2x2 contact sheet of beauty, depth (grey ramp with near/far legend), line and segmentation (palette legend by programme and context class)
Opacity slider that overlays any pass on the beauty capture
modules.method: From the chosen camera render passes with identical size and camera in three.js: (1) clay beauty with ambient occlusion and the CLIM sun (core); (2) linear depth normalised between near and far values around tower plus site; (3) line pass from depth/normal discontinuities plus crease edges; (4) ID pass with flat unlit colour per class (programme tags plus existing-context, approved-tower and other-context classes), no anti-aliasing so tags survive. Passes 2-4 are v1. Save PNGs and a JSON sidecar with camera, sun vector, palette, tag counts and SHA-256. Validate size rules before any API call. For fidelity checks later, depth can be re-estimated from the AI output with Depth Anything V2 Small and compared with the exact depth pass.
modules.human_judgment: Which context to include or hide, time of day and sun angle, which landmarks must remain recognisable, and whether the clay capture is a fair representation of the design.
modules.limits: Only programme tags and the context classes above are semantic; trees, water and street furniture have none. ControlNet checkpoints in the cited examples are trained near 512-1024 px, far below board resolution. OpenAI image edits take reference images, not strict control maps, so passes beyond the beauty capture may be only weak hints.

modules.design_question: Which style and engine give faithful, site-specific, non-generic renderings from the conditioning pack, at what cost, with what fidelity checks and with honest AI labelling?

camera_preset metadata, context tower list and sun vector
programme and materials from ADVANCED mode

cultural and ecological cues from CULT/ECOL packets

parameters.name: engine
parameters.relationship: OpenAI route: image edit from reference images, no explicit depth or line control. Open route (SDXL/Flux + ControlNet via ComfyUI or diffusers): explicit conditioning scale and local control, but licences and GPU needs differ.

parameters.name: openai_model
parameters.relationship: gpt-image-2.5-sunburst (snapshot 2026-09-08) is described for editing precision, gpt-image-2.5-flare for fast generation, gpt-image-2 (snapshot 2026-04-21) remains; all share token prices. A pinned snapshot id reproduces results.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.relationship: Higher quality raises output tokens and cost; earlier models produced 272, 1,056 and 4,160 output tokens at 1024x1024 for low, medium, high, roughly a four-fold step each. Tokens for the 2.5 models are not published in what was read.

parameters.name: size
parameters.relationship: Custom sizes must be multiples of 16 with ratio <= 3:1; above 2560x1440 is experimental. A 3840x2160 output is about 164 px/inch across a 594 mm board, so large heroes may need upscaling.

parameters.name: reference_images
parameters.relationship: gpt-image-2 processes every image input at high fidelity and input_fidelity must be omitted, so each extra reference raises input tokens and cost. The guide's edit example sends four references and states no maximum.

parameters.name: mask_region
parameters.relationship: Masked edits let sky, trees or foreground change while the tower stays; masking is prompt-based and may not follow the mask shape exactly, so protected pixels can still shift.

parameters.name: conditioning_scale (open route)
parameters.relationship: Higher scale keeps output closer to the line/depth guide, lower scale gives more stylistic freedom; the diffusers examples use 0.5. Architecture-specific tuning evidence was not found.

parameters.name: style_preset
parameters.relationship: Style changes how generic an image looks; the brief says to avoid generic, placeless design, so presets should be anchored by site cues (City in Nature, mountains, water) chosen by the team. Effect on jury score is not evidenced.

parameters.name: moderation
parameters.relationship: 'auto' applies standard filtering; blocked requests return moderation_blocked and must not be retried without changing the inputs.

metrics.name: Tower silhouette IoU (fidelity)
metrics.method: Segment the AI output with SAM 2 prompted by the projected tower box, then compare with the tower mask from the conditioning segmentation pass (or use the depth-difference method alone).
metrics.basis: No published benchmark for architectural fidelity; team thresholds, tune on pilot renders.

metrics.name: Line agreement
metrics.good: >= 0.80 of conditioning line pixels within 3 px of an output edge
metrics.method: Edge-detect the output and compute proportion of guide-line pixels with an output edge within a tolerance.
metrics.basis: Team thresholds.

metrics.name: Storey / bay count match (hero views)
metrics.good: visible storey lines equal the model
metrics.method: Human tick in the review step, assisted by overlaying the model's floor lines.
metrics.basis: A rendering must not misrepresent the design; team rule.

metrics.name: Context towers present in output
metrics.good: all existing and approved towers in frame are present (box IoU >= 0.5 with the ID-pass mask) and none invented
metrics.method: SAM 2 masks prompted by each context-tower box, compared with the conditioning ID pass; list differences for the reviewer.
metrics.basis: The brief (as supplied) puts existing and approved towers of 244-305 m in the context; the 0.5 cut-off is a team value.

metrics.name: Lighting consistency
metrics.good: shadows and highlights agree with the CLIM sun vector (human tick against an overlaid arrow)
metrics.method: Reviewer compares the output with the sun-vector overlay; no automated estimator is specified.
metrics.basis: Renders can invent a sun direction; no sourced estimator was found (see unresolved_relationships).

metrics.name: Cost per accepted image
metrics.good: <= team budget set from pilot calls (>= 5 per quality level)
metrics.method: (text_in x 5 + image_in x 8 + image_out x 30) / 10^6 per image at standard rates (batch is half); token counts read from the response usage object.
metrics.basis: Token rates verified; per-image token counts for the 2.5 models are unpublished and edits with references raise input tokens, so the budget must come from logged pilots.

metrics.name: AI label and ledger coverage
metrics.good: 100% of AI-derived images carry a visible caption and a ledger entry
metrics.method: Join render_asset records with board placements.
metrics.basis: Good practice from journal disclosure rules and EU Article 50 principles; Buildner's terms read contain no AI rule.

metrics.name: Provenance signal present in API output
metrics.good: C2PA and/or SynthID detected on the returned image
metrics.method: Read manifest with a C2PA reader; check OpenAI's verification page manually.
metrics.basis: Help-centre text (not opened; search excerpt) says API images carry C2PA metadata and SynthID, with coverage varying and metadata strippable.

visualization: Side-by-side slider of conditioning beauty and AI output with a difference overlay (line mismatches in red, silhouette misses in amber) and a sun-vector arrow
Metric badges (IoU, line agreement, context towers, cost) each linked to the threshold source or an amber 'team assumption' tag
Gallery with 'AI' badge, model snapshot, prompt and cost on each card; running cost meter
modules.method: 1) User picks camera preset, style preset and engine. 2) A structured prompt is built from fields (materials, season, time of day, weather, entourage) with a block-list: no logos, signage, team names, real-person likenesses or imitation of Indigenous art. 3) OpenAI route (core): POST /v1/images/edits with a pinned snapshot, prompt, image[] = clay capture (depth or line only as weak extra references), size, quality; omit input_fidelity on gpt-image-2. Open route (v1): submit a ComfyUI workflow to /prompt (ControlNet depth + line) or call diffusers; keep the seed. 4) Fidelity: SAM 2 segments the output from the projected tower box; compute IoU, line agreement and context-tower presence; overlay the CLIM sun vector for a human lighting check. 5) Ledger row: snapshot, parameters, prompt, input/output hashes, response usage, cost. 6) Attach caption. 7) Human accepts or rejects; rejected renders stay in the ledger.
modules.human_judgment: Whether to use AI imagery at all; style and prompt wording; accepting or rejecting each image; checking that nothing misrepresents the design, sun or context; cultural sensitivity and Indigenous perspectives; rights and tool terms, since Buildner advises against treating AI images as sole work.
modules.limits: OpenAI image edits are not geometry-locked: the guide notes weak precision in layout-sensitive compositions and up to two minutes for complex prompts. Model names and prices were read through a summarising fetch and look unusual; confirm before coding. Renders can invent sun, context or towers, hence the checks. FLUX [dev] weights are non-commercial; fit with Buildner's promotional licence (Terms 12.2) is unchecked.

inputs: M06a: element list, brief_register panel rule, frame and type-size plan

M06b: board_layout (M06a); drawing_set from P13-M02; render_asset from P13-M05 and CLIM/ENER/STRC diagram exports; text_blocks from P13-M08b; ai captions and rights_register from P13-M08a; compass overlays from P13-M03; team deny-list and language allow-list
M06c: submission_status and blocking_issues from P13-M01; two member sign-offs
outputs: M06a: board_layout (frames in mm, element tags, planned text length) consumed by P13-M02, P13-M07 and P13-M01

parameters.name: export_dpi
parameters.relationship: Pixels = mm / 25.4 x dpi: 150 dpi = 3508 x 2480; 200 dpi = 4677 x 3307; 300 dpi = 7016 x 4961. Higher dpi keeps hairlines crisp but pushes JPEG bytes toward the 10 MB cap.

parameters.name: jpeg_quality_search
parameters.relationship: The encoder searches the highest quality that stays under the byte target; lower quality shrinks bytes but adds ringing around thin linework and small type. The curve depends on content, so it is measured, not predicted.

parameters.name: chroma_subsampling
parameters.relationship: 4:2:0 halves chroma resolution and smears thin coloured linework and small coloured type; 4:4:4 keeps them but costs bytes. sharp defaults to 4:2:0; jSquash MozJPEG defaults to progressive with chroma_subsample 2, so set both explicitly.

parameters.name: jpeg_scan_mode
parameters.relationship: Portal handling of progressive JPEG is undocumented, so baseline is the default. Bytes differ by mode and content; measure both on the real board before choosing.

parameters.name: type_scale
parameters.relationship: At fit-to-width on a 1920 px screen, 594 mm = 3.23 px/mm, so 2.5 mm lettering is about 8 px and 3.5 mm about 11 px; smaller text becomes unreadable if the jury views boards on screen (assumed).

parameters.name: placed_image_scale
parameters.relationship: Effective resolution = image width in px / placed width in inches; enlarging an AI render past its native pixels lowers effective dpi and softens detail.

parameters.name: metadata_policy
parameters.unit: strip all | keep IPTC source type
parameters.relationship: Creator names, software strings and manifests can reveal authors, and Terms 5.1 bars identifying marks. sharp removes metadata by default and ExifTool -all= is not guaranteed complete, so every export is re-scanned.

parameters.name: ai_label_placement
parameters.relationship: A visible caption beside each AI-derived image is the operative label; metadata is stripped on export and can be removed anyway. EU AI Act Art. 50 asks for clear, distinguishable disclosure but is marked amended and is only a benchmark.

parameters.name: font_glyph_coverage
parameters.relationship: Nation names need combining marks and modifier letters; a font without them substitutes glyphs and misspells the name. Charis SIL is OFL-licensed and aimed at linguistic text, but coverage must be tested per code point.

parameters.name: deny_list_terms
parameters.relationship: Each added term (member names, university, school, course codes, instructor names, email domains) catches one more possible identifier (Terms 5.1) but can add OCR false positives that block export; reviewers clear a finding with a logged reason.

metrics.name: Bytes per board (hard limit)
metrics.good: <= 10^7 bytes
metrics.method: Measure final file; loop quality and pixel size until under the target.
metrics.basis: Terms 4.8 limit of 10 MB; MB not defined, so the stricter 10^7 bytes is used.

metrics.name: Bytes per board (team target)
metrics.good: <= 9.5 x 10^6 bytes
metrics.method: Same measurement against the margin.
metrics.basis: Team margin for MB/MiB and portal overhead; editable.

metrics.name: File format
metrics.good: JPEG
metrics.method: Magic bytes and extension.
metrics.basis: Terms 4.8.

metrics.name: Pixel ratio
metrics.method: width_px / height_px.
metrics.basis: A2 dimensions verified; landscape comes from the unopened brief; tolerance team-set.

metrics.name: JPEG encoding settings
metrics.good: baseline, 4:4:4, sRGB, no metadata
metrics.bad: progressive or 4:2:0 used without a test
metrics.method: Read SOF sampling factors and scan type from the output file.
metrics.basis: Portal acceptance is undocumented; a live test upload is unsafe, so ask Buildner in Q&A before 3 Nov.

metrics.name: Effective resolution of each placed raster
metrics.good: >= 150 px/inch at 594 mm board width
metrics.method: native px / placed inches for every image.
metrics.basis: Team print/screen target; no jury requirement found.

metrics.name: Smallest text height
metrics.good: >= 3.5 mm on the board (about 11 px at 1920 px width)
metrics.method: Scan text frames and SVG text; report min cap height.
metrics.basis: 2.5 mm and 3.5 mm are nominal lettering sizes in the technical-lettering series; they are not a legibility rule for boards.

metrics.name: Anonymity findings
metrics.good: 0 findings in file name, EXIF/XMP/ICC and OCR text matching the deny-list
metrics.method: Re-read the exported JPEG metadata and OCR tiles of the raster for deny-list strings; seeds include member names, UBC, SALA, ARCH 540, instructors, email domains.
metrics.basis: Terms 5.1: no marks that may identify authority or source; the scan method and seeds are the team's design.

metrics.name: Glyph coverage
metrics.good: 100% of code points in text frames and the allow-list exist in the loaded fonts (NFC-normalised)
metrics.method: Compare each text run's code points with the font cmap before rasterising.
metrics.basis: Team rule to protect Nation names; OCR cannot be relied on for these orthographies.

metrics.name: AI-derived images with visible label
metrics.method: Compare render_asset list with placements and caption frames.
metrics.basis: Disclosure practice; Buildner terms read contain no AI rule.

visualization: WYSIWYG board canvas with snap grid and four-board overview strip

Overlays: text-size heat map (red below 2.5 mm), per-image effective-dpi flags, glyph-fallback markers, byte gauge (bytes against 10^7 and the 9.5 x 10^6 target), anonymity findings pinned to the image
Side-by-side 'what the jury sees' preview at 1920 px width and at 100% zoom
Release strip per board showing gate state (open, passed, signed)
modules.method: M06a stores boards as JSON scenes in mm (frames, element tags, planned text length) and checks the brief's panel rule. M06b composes each scene into one 594 x 420 mm SVG, rasterises with resvg at the chosen dpi, converts to sRGB and encodes MozJPEG (jSquash in a worker or sharp on a server) as baseline 4:4:4 without metadata, lowering quality from 95 toward 70 and then pixel size until under the byte target. It re-reads metadata with ExifTool, OCRs tiles with tesseract.js against the deny-list, checks glyph coverage and writes export_manifest. A proof PDF (1683.8 x 1190.6 pt) is built with pdf-lib for review only. M06c releases the upload package only when P13-M01 reports blocking=false and two members sign.
modules.human_judgment: Composition, narrative order, visual hierarchy and what to show; final QA at 100% zoom; deciding whether captions and disclosures are placed well; font licences; the upload to the Buildner portal and the final anonymity check.
modules.limits: Buildner pixel, colour-mode, progressive and MB/MiB rules are not documented in the pages read; a live-entry test upload is unsafe because the first upload locks edits. Browser canvas size limits were not verified, so use the WASM or server path. JPEG is lossy near the size cap; PDF is a proof only. OCR of Nation-name orthographies is unreliable.

libraries.role: OCR for identifying text (tiles; best effort)

libraries.name: ExifTool
libraries.license: same terms as Perl itself (Artistic or GPL)

libraries.name: Charis SIL
libraries.role: candidate open font for Nation names (coverage to be tested)

modules.name: Jury-criteria self-assessment rubric
modules.design_question: How well do the design and board set address each weighted jury criterion, and what cited evidence supports every self-score?
inputs: jury criteria and sub-criteria with weights 40/30/20/10 (brief, team-supplied)
evidence links to module results from all packets, each with metric, threshold and source
board_layout tags and area share per criterion from P13-M06a
human scores on a 0-4 scale
breach register (departures from policy and guidelines) with rationale from P13-M08a
award tracks: Sustainability Award and Student Award (eligibility text from the brief, not obtained)
outputs: rubric_state: {scores[], evidence[], gaps[], weighted_total, attention_ratio[], award_evidence[]} consumed by P13-M08b and, as advisory gaps, P13-M01
evidence table for the policy reflection

parameters.name: criterion_weights
parameters.relationship: One point on the 0-4 scale is worth 10 points of 100 for human-scale (40%) but 2.5 points for urban integration (10%), so effort and board space should follow the weights. Weights are team-supplied from the brief.

parameters.name: level_descriptors
parameters.relationship: UNRESOLVED: effect of descriptor wording on rater agreement was not found in an opened source (see unresolved_relationships).

parameters.name: evidence_tier
parameters.unit: A measured | B visual | C narrative
parameters.relationship: Higher-tier evidence supports a higher score; a score of 3 or more without tier-A or tier-B evidence is flagged as unsupported (team rule).

parameters.name: board_area_share
parameters.relationship: The share of board area used for a criterion should track its weight; a 30%-weight criterion with 5% area is under-communicated, which matters because the jury sees only the boards.

parameters.name: breach_register
parameters.relationship: The brief says the jury may reward justified breaches of guidelines, so each departure needs a stated reason and evidence; unexplained departures count against the criterion they touch.

parameters.name: award_tracks
parameters.relationship: Sustainability and Student Awards (CAD 1,000 each) are separate prizes; an entry in the top three that wins either takes both prizes. Tracking their evidence (CLIM/ENER results) costs effort but can win a prize.

metrics.name: Weighted self-score
metrics.good: no cut-off: shown as a plain number labelled 'team heuristic'
metrics.method: sum over criteria of weight x score/4 x 100.
metrics.basis: Weights from the brief as supplied by the team; earlier 75/50 cut-offs had no anchor and are removed; the result is not a prediction of jury outcome.

metrics.name: Evidence coverage per criterion
metrics.good: >= 3 items incl. >= 1 measured and >= 1 visual
metrics.method: Count linked evidence by tier.
metrics.basis: Team rule supporting the course requirement to cite sources and show work.

metrics.name: Board attention ratio
metrics.method: (area share of criterion) / (weight share).
metrics.basis: Team heuristic.

metrics.name: Rater disagreement
metrics.good: |score A - score B| <= 1 on the 0-4 scale
metrics.method: Two team members score independently; compare.
metrics.basis: Team threshold; no reliability literature is relied on.

metrics.name: Site-specific evidence count (anti-generic)
metrics.good: >= 3 items tied to the site (landscape, climate, history, Indigenous perspectives) per cultural-context sub-criterion
metrics.method: Count evidence tagged 'site-specific' by the author.
metrics.basis: The brief asks to avoid generic, placeless design; threshold is team-set.

metrics.name: Award evidence (Sustainability Award)
metrics.good: >= 3 linked items incl. >= 1 measured CLIM/ENER result
metrics.method: Count evidence tagged 'sustainability'.
metrics.basis: Award exists (competition page); its judging text is in the brief and was not obtained; threshold is team-set.

visualization: Four-axis radar chart plus a bar whose width follows weight (40/30/20/10); the total is printed as a plain number with a 'team heuristic' label, with no good/bad colouring
Stacked evidence bars per criterion by tier; evidence table with metric, threshold, source link
Board heat strip showing which criterion each element supports; version history of scores
modules.method: Store criteria, sub-criteria, descriptors and evidence links as data. Each evidence item points to a module id, metric name, value, threshold and source id, or to a board element tagged in P13-M06a. Humans enter 0-4 scores with a one-line justification. The tool computes the weighted total, tier counts and board attention ratio and flags: score >= 3 without tier-A/B evidence, criterion with zero evidence, high weight with low area share, large gap between two raters, breaches without rationale (from the P13-M08a register). Optional award tracks list their evidence separately. Scores are never computed or filled by an AI; an optional assistant may only suggest existing results as evidence, and the suggestion is logged. Every threshold shows its source or an amber 'team assumption' tag.
modules.human_judgment: All scores and their interpretation, especially human-scale experience, cultural context and reconciliation, which need lived knowledge and Indigenous perspectives; deciding which breaches to make and justify; interpreting what the jury will value.
modules.limits: No published VTC scoring scale or past jury scores were found; weights are team-supplied from the brief PDF. The jury-panel page lists seven jurors from architecture, engineering and landscape practice and says nothing on scoring. Terms 10.4 describe a shortlist stage before Guest Jury ranking. Self-scores are biased and unvalidated; the rubric measures evidence coverage, not design quality.

parameters.name: assistance_level
parameters.relationship: L0 evidence pack only, L1 outline and questions, L2 critique of a human draft, L3 AI-drafted text (off by default). Higher levels reduce the human share of authorship and raise the disclosure and originality risk.

parameters.name: claim_traceability
parameters.relationship: Each number or policy claim must link to a module result and its source; untraceable numbers are shown as team assumptions or flagged FALSE ASSUMPTION if later disproved, so unsupported claims cannot enter boards silently.

parameters.name: governing_policy_set
parameters.relationship: The 1997 Higher Buildings Policy is under review (Phase 1 early directions; Phase 2 draft policies from fall 2026; no update adopted); protected views are not under review. The reflection must say which document it assesses against.

parameters.name: text_length
parameters.relationship: More words per board lower the type size that fits; the board layout caps legible text, so length trades against the 2.5-3.5 mm text-height targets in P13-M06.

parameters.name: disclosure_detail
parameters.relationship: Journal-style rules require disclosing AI tool use and keep humans responsible for output; a detailed ledger makes the statement accurate and supports the course rule to show work.

parameters.name: identity_exposure
parameters.relationship: A C2PA signing certificate identifies the signer, so signing exported boards with a personal identity would conflict with anonymity; labels use generic visible captions, with IPTC source-type fields kept only in archive copies.

parameters.name: licence_status
parameters.relationship: Terms 4.3 lets Buildner demand image licences, and failure to supply them may disqualify; 12.2 and 12.7 grant Buildner perpetual promotional and publication licences, so each raster needs a licence that allows them. Unknown means blocking.

parameters.name: ai_tool_terms
parameters.relationship: AI outputs carry tool terms and model licences: FLUX [dev] weights are non-commercial, SDXL's Open RAIL++-M allows commercial use with passed-on restrictions, OpenAI terms were not read. Buildner advises against treating AI images as sole work.

parameters.name: explanation_request

metrics.name: Rights register completeness
metrics.good: 100% of placed rasters have source, author, licence, licence URL or evidence hash, and a yes on 'licensable to Buildner under Terms 12.2 and 12.7'
metrics.bad: any raster with unknown licence (blocks release)
metrics.method: Join placements from P13-M06a with register rows; licence pack export lists evidence for each.
metrics.basis: Terms 4.3 (licences on request, failure may disqualify) and 12.2/12.7; the register columns are team design.

metrics.name: Traceable-claim ratio

metrics.method: Regex-detect numbers and policy names; check for a claim link.
metrics.basis: Course requirement to cite sources; cut-offs are team values.

metrics.name: Human-authored share of final text
metrics.good: 100% of final prose typed or edited by a team member (levels L0-L2 only)
metrics.bad: any AI-originated sentence not reviewed and disclosed
metrics.method: Compare diff log provenance tags per paragraph.
metrics.basis: Informed by journal guidance that AI is not an author and humans are accountable; not a Buildner rule.

metrics.name: AI-use ledger completeness
metrics.good: 100% of AI calls (text and image) logged with model, date, purpose, input/output hash
metrics.method: Compare API call log with ledger rows.
metrics.basis: Disclosure principle from ICMJE guidance.

metrics.name: Breach rationale coverage
metrics.good: 100% of flagged breaches have a written justification

metrics.basis: Brief says justified breaches may be rewarded (as supplied by team).

metrics.name: Identifying strings in text
metrics.good: 0 matches against the deny-list
metrics.method: String match; the OCR pass in P13-M06b repeats it on the raster.
metrics.basis: Terms 5.1 bars identifying marks.

metrics.name: IPTC source type on archive copies of AI images
metrics.good: trainedAlgorithmicMedia for generated images; compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia for edits such as inpainting
metrics.bad: absent or wrong in the archive copy

visualization: Three-pane editor: evidence pack with source chips; human draft with provenance underline (none = human, amber = AI-suggested); ledger timeline
Claim linter badges beside each sentence (linked, team assumption, unsupported)
Rights table with a traffic light per board image (known, unknown, restricted) and a licence-pack download
Policy checklist with pass / exceed / breach per policy item and a justification field
modules.method: M08a (upstream of P13-M07): 1) every AI call from P13-M05 writes a JSONL ledger row (model snapshot, date, purpose, input/output hashes, reviewer); 2) rights register: each raster gets source, author, licence, licence URL, evidence hash and a Terms 12.2 answer; unknown licences set blocking in P13-M01; 3) breach entries need a rationale; 4) caption strings are generated for AI images, with IPTC source type only in archive copies. M08b (downstream of P13-M07): 5) evidence pack of module results with source chips; 6) team-authored question templates; 7) the editor stores provenance per paragraph, AI limited to L0-L2; 8) a linter flags numbers or policy names without a claim link; 9) language attested English, Nation names via the allow-list with gloss; 10) text blocks go to P13-M06b.
modules.human_judgment: All prose, positions and ethical stance; whether any AI text is used; reconciliation and Indigenous perspectives, which should draw on community knowledge, not generated text; the final policy reflection; the legal check on rights and tool terms; confirming the course's own AI rules.
modules.limits: No sourced benchmark defines a good policy reflection. Buildner's terms contain no AI rule and its FAQ advises caution, so the team's disclosure standard is a choice. UBC course guidance returned 404. EU AI Act Article 50 is a benchmark only: the explorer marks it amended and shows 2 Aug 2026, but the Digital Omnibus changes were not read; binding force for a Canadian entry is assumed absent.
